page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads. The CPU includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It lacks local NVMe storage and bundled GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. The single-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% on stress-ng tests, and single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance. However, due to the low core count, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng and the bottom 10% for Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 31.35 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 22.01 GB/sec. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput register in the bottom 10%, reflecting limitations in high-throughput concurrent workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highmem-2 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring a larger memory footprint relative to compute power, avoiding the expense of provisioning excess vCPUs. However, the tradeoff is limited parallel processing capability and lower memory bandwidth. This server is best suited for lightweight memory-intensive applications, small-scale databases, basic text processing, single-threaded utility scripts, or development environments that require more than the standard 4 GB of RAM per vCPU but do not demand high computational throughput.
